name: OPEN
aliases: Open urethroplasty versus endoscopic urethrotomy: clarifying the management of men with recurrent urethral stricture
question: In men with recurrent bulbar urethral stricture, does open urethroplasty control voiding symptoms better than endoscopic urethrotomy over 24 months?

design.blinding: open-label; central trial staff masked to allocation
design.population: 222 men with bulbar urethral stricture and at least one previous stricture operation randomized at 38 UK NHS hospitals; two ineligible men were excluded after randomization, leaving 108 and 112 by allocation.
design.locator: AM PDF pp5, 9, Table 1 (p18); arm counts from Table 2 (p19)

verdictNote: Symptom scores did not differ; reintervention was lower after urethroplasty; 39 of 108 urethroplasty patients lacked primary data.
takeaway: In 222 randomized UK men with recurrent bulbar urethral stricture, open urethroplasty and endoscopic urethrotomy did not differ in 24-month voiding symptom score (mean difference -0.36), but urethroplasty had fewer reinterventions (15 versus 29 men; hazard ratio 0.52, 95% CI 0.31 to 0.89).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Goulao B, Carnell S, Shen J, et al. "Surgical Treatment for Recurrent Bulbar Urethral Stricture: A Randomised Open-label Superiority Trial of Open Urethroplasty Versus Endoscopic Urethrotomy (the OPEN Trial)." *Eur Urol.* 2020;78(4):572-580. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2020.06.003
reports.followUp: Symptom score profile over 24 months after randomization; time to reintervention to database closure (at least 24 and up to 48 months)

results.measure: Area-under-the-curve profile of the 0-24 patient-reported voiding symptom score over 24 months (lower is better); adjusted mean difference, urethroplasty minus urethrotomy
results.note: Primary analysis included 69 of 108 and 90 of 112 men. Multiple-imputation intention-to-treat difference -0.33 (95% CI -1.74 to 1.09; p=0.6); modified intention-to-treat -0.52 (95% CI -2.0 to 0.96; p=0.5). No treatment-effect heterogeneity by time since last procedure, age, stricture length or number of previous interventions.

results.measure: Time to first reintervention (hazard ratio, urethroplasty versus urethrotomy); men with at least one reintervention
results.note: Described as the main clinical outcome and powered for a 30% relative reduction (104 men, 90% power). Self-dilatation was not counted as reintervention. Percentages in the monograph (Tables 15 and 17): 16.1% and 27.9% of men with data available. Median (IQR) interval from surgery to reintervention: 474 (399-577) days after urethroplasty versus 308 (211-448) days after urethrotomy.

results.measure: Multiple reintervention events per participant (Andersen-Gill hazard ratio)
results.note: 44 men had at least one reintervention and there were 52 reinterventions overall.

results.measure: Time to first reintervention, per-protocol analysis (men who received the allocated procedure)
results.note: Secondary analysis restricted to men who underwent the allocated procedure.

results.measure: Time to recurrence (hazard ratio, urethroplasty versus urethrotomy); men with recurrence
results.note: Recurrence was a reintervention performed or scheduled, or maximum flow rate or voiding score deteriorated to the pre-intervention value. Counts are among the men who had surgery (93 urethroplasty and 104 urethrotomy; 19 (20.4%) and 39 (37.5%) in the monograph, Table 17).

results.measure: Improvement in Qmax of at least 10 mL/s from baseline at 12 or 24 months (odds ratio, urethroplasty versus urethrotomy)
results.note: At 3 months the odds ratio was 2.1 (95% CI 1.05 to 4.12; p=0.035). The Results text gives 44 and 63 participants with flow-rate data for the 12-24 month comparison; Table 2 prints 18/93 (19%) and 13/104 (13%), whose denominators include 49 and 41 men with missing data (monograph Table 16).

results.endpoint: Impact of urinary symptoms on daily activity
results.measure: Profile score over 24 months (0 none to 3 a lot); adjusted mean difference, urethroplasty minus urethrotomy
Profile score over 24 months; adjusted mean difference, urethroplasty minus urethrotomy
results.note: The Methods describe the scale as 1 (very dissatisfied) to 5 (very satisfied); the Table 1 footnote reverses the direction.

harms.label: Any adverse event (by procedure received)
harms.note: Denominators are men who received urethroplasty (82) or urethrotomy (115). Counts are 82 minus 32 and 115 minus 85 men with no event; 88 events in 80 men overall.

harms.label: Perioperative mouth pain
harms.note: Oral graft harvest site; two men in the urethroplasty group had two events.

harms.label: Erectile dysfunction during follow-up
harms.note: Standalone row; two further urethroplasty patients had erectile dysfunction recorded together with wound infection or wound pain.

harms.label: At least one serious adverse event
harms.note: 22 serious adverse events in 17 men overall; 2 related to the trial intervention and expected. The Discussion text quotes 10.9% versus 11.3%, which does not match Table 4.

harms.label: Death
harms.note: Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, reported as unrelated to the trial intervention.

values.exp: Dorsal graft 45, anastomotic without transection 9, anastomotic with transection 9, ventral graft 7, perineal urethrostomy 1 (of 71)
values.ctl: Dorsal graft 4, anastomotic without transection 4, ventral graft 2, anastomotic with transection 1 (of 11)
Optical cold-knife urethrotomy 90, hot-knife urethrotomy 1, dilatation 2 (of 93)

delivery.label: Started intermittent self-dilatation
delivery.note: All 9 in the urethroplasty group had crossed over to urethrotomy.

delivery.label: Included in the primary symptom analysis
delivery.note: Of those excluded, 15 of 39 (urethroplasty) and 8 of 22 (urethrotomy) had no surgery at all.

delivery.label: Recruitment
delivery.value: 1,262 men identified; 222 randomized between 27 February 2013 and 23 December 2015 at 38 of 53 participating NHS providers

reports.label: NIHR HTA monograph
reports.dateLocator: PMC7750862 (Health Technol Assess 2020 Nov; month only)
reports.citation: Pickard R, Goulao B, Carnell S, et al. "Open urethroplasty versus endoscopic urethrotomy for recurrent urethral stricture in men: the OPEN RCT." *Health Technol Assess.* 2020;24(61):1-110. doi:10.3310/hta24610

results.measure: Mean difference in area under the curve of repeated 0-24 voiding symptom scores
results.note: The monograph abstract prints -1.78 as the lower confidence limit; its results text and tables and the journal report print -1.74. Primary analysis included 69 (63%) of 109 and 90 (80%) of 113 men allocated.

results.measure: Mean (SD) 0-24 voiding symptom score at baseline and 24 months after randomization
Time to reintervention (hazard ratio, urethroplasty versus urethrotomy)

harms.label: Postoperative complications requiring reintervention
harms.note: Counts as printed; the urethrotomy group count includes one death from pulmonary embolism.

reports.label: Cost-effectiveness analysis
reports.citation: Shen J, Vale L, Goulao B, et al. "Endoscopic urethrotomy versus open urethroplasty for men with bulbar urethral stricture: the OPEN randomised trial cost-effectiveness analysis." *BMC Urol.* 2021;21(1):76. doi:10.1186/s12894-021-00836-1

results.measure: Base-case mean total cost in pounds sterling (2017 prices) at 24 months; difference, urethroplasty minus urethrotomy
results.note: Base case, 46 men per group in the cost-utility analysis (Table 3).

results.measure: Base-case mean QALYs at 24 months after randomization (EQ-5D-5L); difference, urethroplasty minus urethrotomy
results.note: Urethrotomy was less costly and at least as effective, so urethroplasty was dominated in the base case.

results.measure: 10-year Markov model base case: total cost in pounds sterling and QALYs per patient
results.note: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio for urethroplasty 301,073 pounds per QALY; the probability that urethroplasty was cost-effective was 2% at a 50,000-pound threshold.

relations.note: Both trials used endoscopic treatment as the comparator in recurrent strictures; ROBUST III tested a paclitaxel-coated balloon, OPEN tested urethroplasty.
